title: Sidewalk Society
statement: "Sidewalk Society" explores how Hanoi's sidewalks become shared living spaces, not only for movement but for eating, gathering, working, and connecting. Since my childhood home is in Hanoi's Old Quarter, I've always felt deeply connected to this way of life. Through scenes of food stalls, plastic stools, and small conversations, the project captures the communal spirit that shapes everyday life in Hanoi.

title: Childhood Reclaim
statement: Living in Saigon, where I get to meet with many city kids, I realized just how few actually got a childhood like mine, tied to the playground and naughty neighbour kids. Time took that away: houses were built, children grew up, and I lost contact with everyone I was close to. Just like the name of the project, I want to reclaim what I once had, and go on a hunt for my childhood amidst the cityscape.

title: The Liminal Self
statement: The Liminal Self is a portrait of a self in suspension, "lung lung" (neither here nor there), trying to remember what they are made of: body, memory, nostalgia, yearning, love, and place. In liminal space identity doesn't disappear all at once; it fades, becomes dim, becomes unknown. The self turns into a shadow that still moves, still feels, still searches for something solid to belong to.

title: how do you remember a person?
statement: I am an artist working with photography and installation, with a focus on time, memory, and cultural experience. This project began from the feeling of distance, not only the physical distance of studying away from home, but the distance created by time and the parts of my family I never fully knew. By photographing my grandparents in their own home, I stepped away from controlled aesthetics and allowed moments of vulnerability, awkwardness, laughter, and waiting to unfold.

title: The Bond
statement: The Bond is a documentary photography project about re (roots) and the reflection of my origins. The photographs were taken during a blessing ceremony called 'Cung An Vi' at my grandmother's house, held after my aunt, who had lived abroad for a long time, finally returned to settle down in Vietnam; the local religious community gathered to pray for my aunt's family's peace at a new place.

title: Bei Jing Li Xiang (Leaving Homeland to Strike Roots in New Soil)
statement: A conceptual photography series built around the eight characters of the Chinese idiom 背井離鄉，落地生根 (leaving one's homeland to strike roots in new soil): Abandon, Well, Leave, Homeland, Settle, New land, Grow, Roots. Each character anchors one stage of the artist's own migration and re-rooting. CURATOR-COMPOSED SUMMARY, please review/edit.
